summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis report (N26) evaluating whether fluoxetine retains a residual cognitive-flexibility/working memory/attention phenotype when SERT (Slc6a4) is genetically knocked out or pharmacologically abolished. The document is a structured research discussion framing a pre-registered experimental claim as NEGATIVE/assumption-kill, noting that no published head-to-head study has demonstrated residual-positive fluoxetine cognitive phenotype under SERT abolish conditions. The report synthesizes prior art (Bengel, Holmes, Brigman, Nikiforuk) and proposes an assay design to test the claim.

content_blocks.title: Document Overview and Hypothesis Identity
content_blocks.content: Mol Labs public report N26 (PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY). Topic: Whether fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotypes survive SERT genetic LOF (Slc6a4) or SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution. Status: NEGATIVE (assumption-kill). Polarity: negative. ip_class: sert-insufficiency. kill_cost_tier=1, time_to_refute=4w. execution_status=NOT_RUN. openlabs_topic: neuroscience-brain. Tags: nootropics, brain-longevity. risk_class: research-discussion.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered acute/subacute rodent (Bengel/Brigman/Nikiforuk-class or Gamo-class) cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention panel with a fluoxetine-alone arm, a SERT genetic LOF (Slc6a4) or SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution, and a fluoxetine-under-abolish arm: under the same condition that abolishes SERT-class attribution, fluoxetine retains residual cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotype ≥50% of fluoxetine-alone (cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention units as pre-specified; α/N pre-specified) — assumption-kill/sert-insufficiency. This is framed as a NEGATIVE claim: no published study has demonstrated this residual-positive result.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content: Fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotypes are commonly attributed to SERT orthosteric blockade. Key prior art: (1) Bengel = Slc6a4/SERT KO tool prior; (2) Holmes 2003 = SERT-null anxiety phenotype prior; (3) Brigman = separate-arm cogn phenocopy/necessity-leaning prior (fluoxetine-WT OR 5-HTT-null improve reversal; NO fluoxetine-in-SERT-KO arm — NOT residual-positive; often AGAINST residual); (4) Nikiforuk = fluoxetine set-shifting phenotype prior. None score residual-positive under SERT abolish. N26 is explicitly distinct from N25 (atomoxetine/NET), N15 (modafinil/DAT), N22 (tyrosine/AMPT), N23 (guanfacine/α2A), N24 (caffeine/A2A), and N16–N21.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Sert-insufficiency assumption-kill: fluoxetine moves cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotypes and is framed as selective SERT blockade. Slc6a4/SERT KO is a validated genetic tool (Bengel). Published flexibility/anxiety phenotype priors exist (Brigman reversal phenocopy; Nikiforuk set-shifting; Holmes 2003 anxiety). No published head-to-head scores residual-positive fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention under Slc6a4 LOF or SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution on the same panel. Preferred approach: cell/slice/block-QC before new animal where a named published abolish-verification system can lock residual first; in vivo Bengel/Brigman/Nikiforuk-class or Gamo-class rodent cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention panel remains the primary kill path.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior art references identified:
1. PMID 9547354 / DOI 10.1124/mol.53.4.649 — Bengel (Mol Pharmacol 1998): Serotonin-transporter-deficient mice (5-HTT−/−); high-affinity [³H]5-HT uptake absent in 5-HTT−/−; MDMA locomotor effect abolished. KO tool prior; NO fluoxetine cogn residual-under-abolish arm.
2. PMID 14653308 / DOI 10.1046/j.1601-1848.2003.00050.x — Holmes (Genes Brain Behav 2003): SERT-null mutant anxiety-related behavior (background-dependent). KO anxiety phenotype prior; NO fluoxetine cogn residual arm.
3. PMID 20032063 / DOI 10.1093/cercor/bhp266 — Brigman (Cereb Cortex 2010): Pharmacological (chronic fluoxetine in C57BL/6J) OR genetic (5-HTT null) SERT inactivation improves reversal learning. Cogn phenocopy/necessity-leaning; arms tested separately; NO fluoxetine-in-SERT-KO residual arm; NOT residual-positive; often AGAINST residual.
4. PMID 20580164 / DOI 10.1016/j.psyneuen.2010.06.001 — Nikiforuk (Psychoneuroendocrinology 2011): Antidepressants incl. fluoxetine alleviate stress-induced ED set-shifting deficit; also promote flexibility in unstressed rats. Fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility phenotype prior; NO SERT-abolish residual arm.
Additionally noted (promoted, OUT of public prior_art): PMID 12464448 — Holmes (Neuropsychopharmacology 2002): Fluoxetine anti-immobility abolished in 5-HTT−/− on TST — antidepressant necessity AGAINST residual for that endpoint; NOT cogn-flexibility/WM/attention residual H2H.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Under SERT genetic LOF (Slc6a4) or SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution, fluoxetine still retains cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotype on the same panel — OR Brigman 20032063 already proves residual fluoxetine under SERT abolish — OR Bengel/Holmes/Nikiforuk already constitute residual-under-abolish or cogn-panel genetic necessity-abolish H2H — OR Holmes 12464448 TST abolish already is cogn residual — OR N15–N25 already settle residual fluoxetine under SERT abolish.

Baseline measured: All four prior art references (Bengel, Holmes, Brigman, Nikiforuk) confirmed as LITERATURE without fluoxetine cogn residual-under-abolish arm. Matched residual-positive fluoxetine under Slc6a4 LOF or SERT-matched block: UNKNOWN (soft-complete Q_resid_tight NON-MATCH residual-positive; Q_brigman_arms confirms no fluox×KO residual arm; cogn-panel genetic necessity-abolish H2H NOT FOUND). Residual fluoxetine phenotype ≥50% of fluoxetine-alone when SERT-class attribution abolished: PREDICTION only.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. N1–N25 do NOT prove N26 — especially N25 (SERT ≠ NET; fluoxetine ≠ atomoxetine), N15 (DAT ≠ SERT), N22 (AMPT ≠ SERT LOF), N23 (α2 ≠ SERT), N24 (A2A ≠ SERT). Soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated residual gain.
2. Necessity-leaning phenocopy FOUND — Brigman 20032063 constrains SERT bridge (separate-arm phenocopy; often AGAINST residual) — PRIOR_ART PARTIAL OK, not auto-REJECT. Do NOT invent residual-positive H2H; do NOT treat Brigman as residual-positive; do NOT treat Holmes 12464448 TST abolish as cogn residual; do NOT invent cogn-panel genetic necessity-abolish H2H.
3. Prefer cell/slice/block-QC before new animal; lock same-panel acute/subacute rodent (Bengel/Brigman/Nikiforuk-class or Gamo-class) cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention with fluoxetine ± Slc6a4 LOF or SERT-matched challenge as primary kill path; no dosing; NOT MB/MAOI; not N15–N25 clones; orthosteric_drift=false.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three ablation conditions identified:
1. Remove same-panel contrast of residual fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotype under Slc6a4 LOF or SERT-matched blockade: Without the abolish×residual H2H on a Bengel/Brigman/Nikiforuk-class or Gamo-class panel with a fluoxetine arm, separate phenocopy/necessity-leaning LITERATURE and phenotype/tool LITERATURE cannot show sert-insufficiency as a residual-positive kill.
2. Remove verified abolish gate (Slc6a4 LOF or SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution) plus fluoxetine-alone comparator as the residual gate: Without verified SERT-class abolish and fluoxetine-alone comparator under the same condition, residual fluoxetine is just 'another monoamine agent under nonspecific challenge,' not an assumption-kill of SERT-class sufficiency.
3. Remove N15≠N26 through N25≠N26 discipline plus Brigman-not-residual-positive and Holmes-TST≠cogn-residual discipline: Treating adjacent residuals (N15–N25) or phenocopy as residual-under-abolish would invent an H2H result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Refute if: On the pre-registered acute/subacute rodent (Bengel/Brigman/Nikiforuk-class or Gamo-class) cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention panel, under Slc6a4 genetic LOF or a SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution, residual fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotype falls below 50% of fluoxetine-alone (cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention units as pre-specified) — so SERT-class sufficiency for the fluoxetine phenotype survives and sert-insufficiency fails — when abolish-gate, fluoxetine-alone comparator, and power/assay artifacts that would otherwise leave the test inconclusive are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Execution and IP Status
content_blocks.content: execution_status=NOT_RUN. fto_status=UNKNOWN. ip_class=sert-insufficiency. kill_cost_tier=1. time_to_refute=4w. vault_hold=no. Related priors: N15 (modafinil-DAT residual ≠ fluoxetine×SERT; DAT ≠ SERT); N16 (plasma-Cr/PCr ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N17 (Hericium×NGF/TrkA ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N18 (theanine-adenosine ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N19 (Rhodiola-HPA ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N20 (Bacopa×AChE ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N21 (nicotine×nAChR ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N22 (tyrosine/AMPT ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N23 (guanfacine×alpha2 ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N24 (caffeine×A2A ≠ fluoxetine×SERT); N25 (atomoxetine×NET ≠ fluoxetine×SERT; ESPECIALLY DISTINCT). N2 holds sole ip_class=none. N1–N25 ≠ proof.

key_findings: No published head-to-head study has demonstrated residual-positive fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotype under SERT genetic LOF (Slc6a4) or SERT-matched blockade that abolishes SERT-class attribution — matched residual H2H is UNKNOWN.
Bengel (PMID 9547354): 5-HTT−/− mice show absent high-affinity [³H]5-HT uptake and abolished MDMA locomotor enhancement — validated SERT KO tool, but no fluoxetine cogn residual-under-abolish arm.
Holmes (PMID 14653308): SERT-null mutant mice show background-dependent anxiety phenotype — KO anxiety phenotype prior, no fluoxetine cogn residual arm.

Brigman (PMID 20032063): Chronic fluoxetine in C57BL/6J OR 5-HTT null (separate arms) both improve reversal learning — cogn phenocopy/necessity-leaning; NO fluoxetine-in-SERT-KO residual arm; often AGAINST residual-under-SERT-LOF.

Nikiforuk (PMID 20580164): Fluoxetine alleviates stress-induced ED set-shifting deficit and promotes flexibility in unstressed rats — fluoxetine cognitive-flexibility phenotype prior; no SERT-abolish residual arm.

Holmes (PMID 12464448, promoted/out of public prior_art): Fluoxetine anti-immobility abolished in 5-HTT−/− on TST — antidepressant necessity AGAINST residual for that endpoint; NOT cogn-flexibility/WM/attention residual H2H.

Claim is pre-registered as NEGATIVE (assumption-kill): the hypothesis predicts fluoxetine retains ≥50% residual cognitive-flexibility/WM/attention phenotype under SERT abolish, but this is a PREDICTION not yet tested (execution_status=NOT_RUN).
Refutation threshold: residual fluoxetine phenotype <50% of fluoxetine-alone under verified SERT-class abolish would confirm SERT-class sufficiency and refute sert-insufficiency.
Competing inconclusive outcomes pre-registered: abolish condition fails to kill SERT-class attribution, fluoxetine-alone null, underpowered strata, or assay-identity mismatch.
kill_cost_tier=1, time_to_refute=4w — low-cost, rapid experimental resolution proposed; preferred approach is cell/slice/block-QC before new animal.
N25 (atomoxetine/NET) is especially distinct from N26 (fluoxetine/SERT): SERT ≠ NET; fluoxetine ≠ atomoxetine — prior series results do not transfer.
PRIOR_ART PARTIAL: necessity-leaning phenocopy FOUND (Brigman); residual-positive under abolish ABSENT; phenotype/tool priors FOUND — soft-complete empty ≠ novelty/≠ failure.
